NONE: › used to form the present participle of regular verbs
（用以構成規則動詞的現在分詞）

example: calling
叫
asking
問

NONE: › (of a person) very intelligent and skilful, or (of a thing) skilfully made or planned and involving new ideas and methods
（人）靈巧的；（物品等）製作精巧的；（方法等）巧妙的

example: an ingenious idea/method/solution
巧妙的主意／方法／解決辦法
Johnny is so ingenious - he can make the most remarkable sculptures from the most ordinary materials.
強尼真是手巧——他可以用最普通的材料製作出最棒的雕塑。

NONE: › a young woman who has little experience and is very trusting, especially as played in films and plays
（尤指電影或戲劇中）天真無邪的少女
› someone's ability to think of clever new ways of doing something
心靈手巧；足智多謀；獨創力

example: Drug smugglers constantly use their ingenuity to find new ways of getting drugs into a country.
毒販總是絞盡腦汁地尋找跨境販毒的新花招。

NONE: › honest, sincere, and trusting, sometimes in a way that seems silly
天真的；胸無城府的

example: It has to be said it was rather ingenuous of him to ask a complete stranger to take care of his luggage.
他讓一個完全陌生的人幫自己看管行李，這未免也太天真了。

NONE: › to eat or drink something
攝取，嚥下（食物）

example: The chemicals can be poisonous if ingested.
這些化學製品如果攝入體內可能會引起中毒。

NONE: › the process of absorbing nutrients or medications into the body by eating or drinking them
攝取（營養，藥物）

example: There is a therapy option that does not require the ingestion of drugs.
有一種不需要攝取藥物的治療方案。

NONE: › a partly closed space by a large open fireplace built so that you can sit close to the fire
壁爐邊；壁爐旁的角落
› that people should be ashamed of because it is not fair or honest
不光彩的，可恥的

example: That country has a long, inglorious record of dealing harshly with political prisoners.
那個國家因為長期虐待政治犯而留下不光彩的紀錄。

NONE: › a piece of metal, usually in the shape of a narrow brick
錠；鑄塊

example: a gold/silver ingot
金錠／銀錠

NONE: › to establish something such as a belief so firmly that it is not likely to change
使…深深印在腦中；使根深蒂固

example: We want to ingrain good financial habits in people.
我們想讓人們腦中有很強的理財好習慣。

NONE: › (of beliefs) so firmly held that they are not likely to change
（觀念）根深蒂固的
› Ingrained dirt has got under the surface of something and is difficult to remove.
（塵土等）深嵌著的，難以去除的

example: Such ingrained prejudices cannot be corrected easily.
如此根深蒂固的偏見是不容易糾正的。
The belief that you should own your house is deeply ingrained in our society.
在我們的社會中，應該擁有自己的住房這一觀念根深蒂固。
The oil had become ingrained in his skin.
油污已滲入他的皮膚。

NONE: › a person who is not grateful
忘恩負義者
› to make someone like you by praising or trying to please them
討好，奉承

example: He's always trying to ingratiate himself with his boss.
他總是設法討好老闆。

NONE: › Ingratiating behaviour is intended to make people like you.
迎合的，奉承的

example: an ingratiating smile/manner
諂媚的微笑／舉止

NONE: › the fact that someone is not grateful for something
忘恩負義
B1 a food that is used with other foods in the preparation of a particular dish
（食品的）成分，材料
B2 one of the parts of something successful
（成功的）要素，因素

example: The list of ingredients included 250 g of almonds.
清單上列出的材料包括250克的杏仁。
Trust is a vital ingredient in a successful marriage.
信任是婚姻幸福的重要因素。

NONE: › the act of entering something
進入

example: There had been an ingress of water into the site.
場地進水了。

NONE: › growing into the flesh
向內生長的，長進肉裡的

example: She's having an operation on an ingrowing toenail.
她因趾甲長到肉裡正在動手術。
an ingrowing hair
向內長的毛髮

NONE: › relating to the groin (= the part of the body where the legs join the body)
腹股溝的，鼠蹊的

example: Inflammation of the inguinal nodes can be often linked to cancers in the genital tract or anal canal.
鼠蹊淋巴結發炎通常可以與生殖器道和肛管癌症聯繫起來。
